title: CIA-UAP-D024, Approval in Principle Research Concerned with UFOs, 1952
description: A 1952 CIA routing sheet and memorandum seeking the Deputy Director's approval in principle for an outside research project on unidentified flying objects, run through the Office of Scientific Intelligence.

title: CIA-UAP-D025, Proposal to Consider Psychological Warfare Implications of UFO Related Issues, 1952
description: A 1952 memorandum from CIA Director Walter B. Smith to the Psychological Strategy Board, transmitting a proposal to the National Security Council that unidentified flying objects 'appear to have implications for psychological warfare as well as for intelligence and operations,' and suggesting the board discuss possible offensive or defensive uses of the phenomena.

title: CIA-UAP-D026, Summary Assessment of Flying Saucers, 1952
description: An August 1952 CIA overall evaluation of 'flying saucers': of the 1,000 to 2,000 reports the Air Force had received, a large share were judged 'phoney' or explained as known aircraft, balloons and natural phenomena, leaving fewer than 100 reasonably credible reports unexplained.

title: CIA-UAP-D027, Office of Scientific Intelligence Briefing on Flying Saucers, 1952
description: The CIA Office of Scientific Intelligence's 14 August 1952 briefing on flying saucers, given after a surge of reports and a White House query: a history beginning with Kenneth Arnold's 1947 sighting of nine discs near Mount Rainier, an analysis of the Air Force's investigations, and theories about the unexplained cases.

title: CIA-UAP-D028, Assessment of National Security Issues Relating to Flying Saucers, 1952
description: An October 1952 CIA memorandum assessing national-security issues raised by flying saucers: whether the objects could be an attack on the U.S., and the risk that an enemy could exploit the public confusion to use some air weapon.

title: CIA-UAP-D029, Official Diary Entry on Flying Saucers, 1952
description: An October 1952 entry from a senior CIA official's official diary: a colleague reports new information on flying saucers, 'particularly reports of sightings on the ground by relatively reliable observers,' and notes that a key puzzle in the reports so far was the lack of noise.

title: DOW-UAP-D165, Unresolved Radar Detection, North America, 2023
description: A 2023 civil air-surveillance radar track: eight detections over 84 seconds at an estimated 55,000 to 70,000 feet. If they were one object, it covered about 38.5 miles, roughly 1,650 mph (about Mach 2.5), with a 39-degree turn; the report cautions that the 12-second radar sweep cannot establish that all eight detections were the same object.

title: DOW-UAP-D172, BAASS Ten Month Report, July 2009
description: The July 2009 Ten Month Report from Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS), the contractor for the Pentagon-funded Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP): 538 pages on the program's organization, its UAP investigations and its research projects.

title: DOW-UAP-D182, AAWSAP Statement of Work, August 2008
description: The August 2008 Defense Intelligence Agency solicitation that created the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program, seeking studies of advanced aerospace technologies and threats out to 40 years in the future.

title: DOW-UAP-D183, Correspondence from Senator Harry Reid, June 24 2009
description: A June 24, 2009 letter from Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid to Deputy Secretary of Defense William Lynn about the DIA's advanced aerospace threat studies (AATIP), asking him to establish a 'Restricted Special-Access-Program' with a restricted access list for parts of the program.

title: DOW-UAP-D184, AAWSAP Talking Paper for Senator Reid Engagement, May 2009
description: A May 2009 DIA talking paper preparing the agency's director for a visit from Senator Harry Reid, summarizing the status of the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications contract and Reid's interest in 'unconventional aerospace technologies.'

title: DOW-UAP-D185, Review of AAWSAP Special Access Program Request, November 2009
description: A November 2009 DIA information memo evaluating Senator Harry Reid's request to make the advanced aerospace program, which his letter called the Advanced Aerospace Threat and Identification Program, a restricted special access program.

title: DOW-UAP-D186, DIA Information Memorandum on AATIP AAWSAP, December 2010
description: A December 2010 information memo from DIA Director Lt. Gen. Ronald Burgess on the Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program, first funded with a $10 million congressional add sponsored by Senators Reid and Inouye.

title: DOW-UAP-D187, DIA Talking Paper for Senator Reid Engagement, January 2009
description: A January 2009 DIA talking paper preparing the agency's director for Senator Harry Reid's visit, summarizing the advanced aerospace weapon applications contract.

title: DOW-UAP-D188, Review of AAWSAP Contract Deliverables, October 2009
description: An October 2009 DIA review of the quality and value of the first-year technical reports delivered by Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies under the advanced aerospace contract.

title: DOW-UAP-D189, Air Intelligence Information Report, Virginia, 1957
description: A November 1957 Air Force intelligence report from Virginia: observers trying to spot Sputnik saw a small black speck move directly overhead.

title: DOW-UAP-D190, Air Intelligence Information Report, Massachusetts, 1957
description: An October 1957 Air Force intelligence report: an Air Force Reserve captain, his brother and three companions on a fishing trip off Woods Hole, Massachusetts reported a cylindrical object with protrusions on its front, rear and sides.

title: DOW-UAP-D191, Air Intelligence Information Report, Texas, 1957
description: The Air Force investigation of the November 1957 Levelland, Texas sightings: an oval object about 200 feet long, which two witnesses said hovered or rested on the ground for three to five minutes, with statements from residents, the county sheriff and a patrolman.

title: DOW-UAP-D192, Air Intelligence Information Report, Nebraska, 1957
description: A November 1957 Air Force intelligence report on Reinhold Schmidt of Kearney, Nebraska, who told city officials he found an unusual object on the ground, spoke with its six crew members and spent 30 minutes inside it, with the Air Force's investigation and the preparing officer's comments.

title: DOW-UAP-D193, Air Intelligence Information Report, New Mexico, 1957
description: A November 1957 Air Force intelligence report on an unidentified flying object seen on two occasions by two separate Army military-police patrols near Stallion Site Camp, about 90 miles north of White Sands Proving Ground headquarters, New Mexico.

title: DOW-UAP-D194, Air Intelligence Information Report, New Mexico, 1957
description: A November 1957 Air Force intelligence report on an object seen by James W. Stokes, an electronics technician at the Air Force Missile Development Center, while driving US Highway 54 south of Orogrande, New Mexico on 4 November 1957.

title: DOW-UAP-D195, Air Intelligence Information Report, New Mexico, 1957
description: A November 1957 Air Force intelligence report on an object seen from the control tower at Kirtland Air Force Base, New Mexico, by two airways operations specialists at about 10:45 p.m. on 4 November 1957.

title: DOW-UAP-D196, Air Intelligence Information Report, Washington, 1957
description: A 1957 Air Force intelligence report: a bright, silvery, circular object 'like the sun' seen southwest of Moses Lake, Washington, which at times seemed to split and then reform.

title: DOW-UAP-D197, Air Intelligence Information Report, Michigan, 1957
description: A 1957 Air Force intelligence report from Monroe County, Michigan: stargazers by Lake Erie saw what looked like a meteorite level off at about 1,500 feet and pass 150 yards in front of them at about 225 mph.

title: DOW-UAP-D198, Air Intelligence Information Report, Japan, 1957
description: A November 1957 Air Force intelligence information report on an unidentified flying object reported over Japan.

title: DOW-UAP-D199, Air Intelligence Information Report, Iran, 1957
description: A 1957 Air Force intelligence report from Tehran: a U.S. Army attache office sergeant, his wife and servant watched a high vapor trail, estimated above 60,000 feet, cross the city from east to west for three and a half minutes.

title: DOW-UAP-D200, Air Intelligence Information Report, Peru, 1957
description: A 1957 Air Force intelligence report on two sightings in Peru within two weeks, including an aqua-colored object that emitted sparks before apparently falling to earth in the Talavera district.

title: DOW-UAP-D201, Air Intelligence Information Report, Iran, 1957
description: A November 1957 report relaying a message from the American consul in Tabriz: unidentified flying objects had been sighted over Azerbaijan on several occasions during the previous six months.

title: DOW-UAP-D202, Air Intelligence Information Report, Peru, 1957
description: A 1957 Air Force intelligence report from Peru: a qualified weather observer tracked an unidentified flying object with an automatic Zeiss recording theodolite on four dates between 26 October and 8 November 1957.

title: DOW-UAP-D203, Air Intelligence Information Report, California, 1957
description: A 1957 Air Force intelligence report on an unidentified object seen by James S. Hilbe on two mornings near Upland, California.

title: DOW-UAP-D204, Air Intelligence Information Report, Virginia, 1957
description: A November 1957 Air Force intelligence report: three residents of Abingdon, Virginia reported a glowing object high in the sky on 6 November 1957, which appeared somewhat differently to each of them.

title: DOW-UAP-D205, Air Intelligence Information Report, Japan, 1956
description: A December 1956 Air Force report from Japan: two USAF F-86D pilots on a practice mission tracked something resembling the upper half of a sphere on radar for seven to eight minutes and saw it on and off for three to four minutes; they could not close within five nautical miles, and its radar return left the scope at an estimated 1,500 to 1,800 knots.

title: DOW-UAP-D206, Unresolved UAP Report, California, 1953
description: A December 1953 sighting over Agoura, California reported by Clarence L. 'Kelly' Johnson, chief engineer of Lockheed, and his associates, forwarded to the Air Technical Intelligence Center with a note that Johnson was reluctant to write it up. The Air Force record card concluded it was a lenticular cloud.

title: DOW-UAP-D207, Unresolved UAP Report, California, 1956
description: Project Blue Book records of August 1956 sightings by three civilians in Fontana and La Jolla, California: brilliant red objects with fiery, comet-like tails and two yellow-white lights.

title: DOW-UAP-D208, Unresolved UAP Report, California, 1965
description: Project Blue Book records of an August 1965 sighting at Palos Verdes, California: two boys watching through a telescope saw a round object with red, white and blue flashing lights moving back and forth across Catalina faster than an aircraft.

title: DOW-UAP-D209, Unresolved UAP Report, California, 1955
description: Project Blue Book records of a March 1955 sighting from Catalina Island, California: a very bright round object that changed from orange to red and fell straight down; the Air Force concluded it was probably a meteor.

title: DOW-UAP-D210, Unresolved UAP Report, California, 1957
description: Project Blue Book records of a November 1957 object seen across Southern California within minutes, from San Clemente Island to San Bernardino; the Air Force concluded it was a meteor.

title: DOW-UAP-D211, Unresolved UAP Report, California, 1956
description: Project Blue Book records of an August 1956 sighting in Fontana, California: one round red object with a tail, the size of a basketball at arm's length, that faded into fog after two minutes.

title: DOW-UAP-D212, Unresolved UAP Report, California, 1966
description: Project Blue Book records of a 1966 sighting at San Pedro, California: two witnesses watched a light brighter than the brightest star, white with a red center, move northwest and fade slowly over about five minutes; the Air Force listed it as a possible hot-air balloon.

title: DOW-UAP-D213, Unresolved UAP Report, California, 1949
description: Project Blue Book records of a June 1949 sighting in Glendale, California: two bright, metallic, oval objects that caught the sun, approached from the northeast and flew off into the distance; the Air Force concluded they were aircraft.
